units.title: Inventions
units.intro: Grammar: basic paragraphing II (developing paragraphs) and adverbs of frequency, including negative ones (seldom, rarely, hardly ever).

cards.title: Developing paragraphs
rule: Paragraphs can be developed by **examples**, **cause and effect** (*because, as a result*), **comparison and contrast** (*similarly, whereas, on the other hand*), or **process / time order** (*first, next, finally*).
Example: *The mobile phone has changed communication. **For example**, ... **As a result**, ...*

examples.text: The printing press spread knowledge. As a result, more people learned to read.
Whereas used to show a result.
examples.fix: Use as a result / therefore for results; whereas for contrast.

cards.title: Forms and examples
head: Adverb
Approx. frequency
Example
rows: The sun always rises in the east.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Since the local library was renovated last year, the number of visitors ________ significantly.

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** The subject is 'the number of visitors' (singular).
The sentence describes an action that started in the past (renovated last year) and continues to have relevance in the present, requiring the present perfect tense (has/have + V3).
**Step 2: Watch out for the trap.** Students often see 'visitors' (plural) and choose 'have increased'.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The science teacher asked Dawit, 'Why ________ your assignment on time yesterday?'

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** This is a direct question in the past simple tense.
Questions require subject-auxiliary inversion: Wh-word + auxiliary (didn't) + Subject (you) + base verb (complete).
**Step 2: Watch out for the trap.** Option A incorrectly combines 'didn't' with the past tense verb 'completed'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The rare African manuscript ________ from the national archives before the guards noticed the broken window.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
The sentence describes two past events: the manuscript being stolen and the guards noticing the broken window. The theft happened before the guards noticed it, requiring the past perfect passive voice (had been + V3).

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Option A ('was stolen') is simple past passive. While grammatically correct in isolation, it does not correctly sequence the two past actions. Option D ('has been stolen') is present perfect, which cannot be paired with the simple past past clause ('before the guards noticed').

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
እዚ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ክልተ ኣብ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ዝተፈጸሙ ድርጊታት የነጻጽር። እቲ ጽሑፍ ዝተሰረቐሉ ግዜ፡ እቶም ሓለውቲ ቅድሚ ምርኣዮም ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ካብቲ ሓደ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ንላዕሊ ዝቐደመ (earlier past) እዩ። ስለዚ ሕሉፍ ፍጹም ጥንሳዊ መዋቕር (past perfect passive) 'had been stolen' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Each of the candidates who applied for the engineering position ________ a written test.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
The subject of the sentence is 'Each' (singular), which always takes a singular verb and auxiliary (Each → singular verb).

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Students often look at the plural noun closest to the verb ('candidates') and incorrectly select the plural auxiliary 'have' (Option B) or 'are' (Option C). This is a classic subject-verb agreement trap.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'Each' (ነፍሲ ወከፍ) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ነጸላ (singular) እዩ። ስለዚ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ነጸላ ግሲ 'has to take' (Option A) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። 'candidates' (ሕጹያት) ዝብል ቃል ብዙሕ ስለ ዝኾነ 'have' ምምራጽ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which sentence develops a paragraph by giving a reason?

options.D: The bicycle is popular in Asmara because the roads are flat in many areas and it is cheap to use.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** A reason answers "why?".

**Step 2:** Option D explains why the bicycle is popular (flat roads, low cost).

**Step 3:** The others are simple facts or unrelated.

**Tip:** Develop a paragraph with examples, reasons, facts, comparison or process steps. Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) go before the main verb but after "be".

cards.title: Adverbs of frequency
rule: From most to least: **always, usually, often, sometimes, seldom/rarely, hardly ever, never**.
Position: **before** the main verb (*I **often** use a computer*) but **after** be (*She is **always** late*) and after the first auxiliary (*I have **never** seen it*).
**seldom, rarely, hardly ever, never** already have a negative meaning, so do NOT add *not*: *I **hardly ever** watch TV* (not *I don’t hardly ever*).
cards.pattern: subject + adverb + main verb  ·  be + adverb

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "He doesn’t rarely go out."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** From most to least: **always, usually, often, sometimes, seldom/rarely, hardly ever, never**.
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "He doesn’t rarely go out." breaks this rule.
**Check:** Position: **before** the main verb (*I **often** use a computer*) but **after** be (*She is **always** late*) and after the first auxiliary (*I have **never** seen it*).

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **Seldom, rarely, hardly, never are already NO** — never add not.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Develop paragraphs with examples, cause and effect, comparison/contrast or process order. Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb, after be and after the first auxiliary; seldom, rarely, hardly ever and never are negative already.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following is a **correctly** inverted statement?

options.A: Hardly I have seen a chameleon.
options.B: Had the boy wrote never to his sister.
options.C: No sooner had Hanna hung up the phone than it rang again.
options.D: I seldom wear a hat in the winter.

cards.why:
Inversion occurs when the auxiliary verb comes before the subject, often after negative adverbs. 
- A is wrong (should be 'Hardly **have I** seen'). 
- B is wrong (should be 'The boy had never written'). 
- C is correct: **'No sooner'** + **'had'** (auxiliary) + **'Hanna'** (subject) + **'than'**.

cards.title: Quick check

options.A: They always are kind to visitors.
options.B: They are always kind to visitors.
options.C: Always they kind are to visitors.
options.D: They are kind always to visitors.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Adverbs of frequency come after "be".

**Step 2:** "are always" is correct.

**Step 3:** The other positions are wrong in standard English.

**Tip:** Develop a paragraph with examples, reasons, facts, comparison or process steps. Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) go before the main verb but after "be".

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which adverb shows the lowest frequency?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The scale runs: always – usually – often – sometimes – rarely – never.

**Step 2:** "never" means 0%.

**Step 3:** So it shows the lowest frequency.

**Tip:** Develop a paragraph with examples, reasons, facts, comparison or process steps. Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) go before the main verb but after "be".

glossary.meaning: Two negatives in one clause; incorrect in standard English.
